RagShortTexts: The House of Vítkovci bore the five-petaled rose, commanding southern Bohemia under Vok I.

Variants.Content: The Slavic House of Vítkovci dominated southern Bohemia, divided into branches bearing the famous five-petaled rose. Led by Vok I of Rožmberk (Rosenberg), who carried a red rose on argent, the family garrisoned Krumlov and Rožmberk castles along the Upper Vltava River, serving as High Marshal of the Kingdom of Bohemia under Ottokar II.
While commanding Přemyslid royal hosts across Austria and Prussia, the Rožmberks guarded traditional baronial liberties against centralizing crown encroachment.
The red rose banner flies above Český Krumlov. The lords patronized Cistercian monks at Vyšší Brod, erecting mills and safeguarding rural communities from external tax extortions.
